title: Coconut Leaf Beetle (Brontispa): Signs, Damage and Control
metaTitle: Coconut Leaf Beetle: Brontispa Damage and Control
metaDescription: The coconut leaf beetle, Brontispa, chews the young spear leaf and leaves brown streaks. Learn the signs and the wasps and fungi that control it.
excerpt: The coconut leaf beetle, Brontispa longissima, hides in the unopened spear leaf and chews it into brown streaks. As the leaf opens, the damage turns into grey and scorched blotches. This page shows how to recognize it and why natural enemies work better than repeated spraying.

heroImage.credit: Cameron Brumley, DAFWA, CC BY 3.0 AU, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text:
Brontispa is a small, narrow beetle, only 8 to 10 mm long. The adults and the larvae both feed on the soft tissue of the youngest leaf, still folded in the center of the palm. Coconut is the main host. It also attacks betel nut, sago palm, oil palm and many ornamental palms.

The beetle came into the Philippines on shipments of ornamental plants. It was first seen around 2005. From August 2007 to March 2011, PCARRD reports, it affected more than three million coconut palms. Since coconut supports about 3.5 million farmers, the beetle is a serious worry.

blocks.caption: Quick facts
rows: It attacks palms of all ages, and the damage to nursery seedlings and newly planted palms is often severe. Dry periods favor it.

The whole life cycle happens inside the unopened spear leaf. Eggs hatch in 4 to 5 days, the larvae feed for about 4 weeks, and adults live about 7 months. Long distance spread follows the movement of palms and plants by people.

blocks.text: How to Identify Coconut Leaf Beetle

Open a young spear leaf and look at the folded surfaces. You will find narrow flat beetles and flat, pale larvae feeding side by side. The leaflets show narrow red brown streaks along the midrib. When the leaf opens, the streaks join into grey, scorched blotches. Wind or drought damage does not come with live insects inside the spear.

items: Narrow red brown streaks run along the leaflets of the unopened spear leaf.
As the leaf opens, the streaks grow into grey, scorched blotches.
The youngest fronds look burned, while the older fronds stay green.
Flat, narrow beetles and larvae hide inside the folded spear leaf.
Seedlings in the nursery and young palms show the worst damage.

blocks.title: Do not confuse it with
blocks.text: Brontispa damage can resemble the scorched look of [cocolisap](/pests/cocolisap) and of drought. Cocolisap shows scales on the underside of open leaflets. Brontispa shows live beetles and larvae inside the unopened spear.
How Coconut Leaf Beetle Hurts Your Crop

A severe attack can kill the palm. Palms that survive are weaker against drought and disease, and the yield of bearing palms drops a lot. In Cambodia, an outbreak attacked about 58 percent of the palms and killed 16 percent, according to an APPPC report. In the Philippines, more than three million palms were affected between August 2007 and March 2011.

Spraying gave only short relief. The beetle came back as soon as the spray wore off. That is why the PCA moved to integrated pest management, with biological control at the center.
How to Control Coconut Leaf Beetle

items: Inspect nursery seedlings and young palms often. Open the spear leaf and look for beetles and larvae.
Remove and destroy badly damaged young leaves and seedlings that are full of larvae, so they stop feeding the next generation.
Use the larval parasitoid wasp Asecodes hispinarum. The PCA and research teams are testing and releasing it in the Philippines.
Use the pupal parasitoid Tetrastichus brontispae where it is available. It was introduced successfully in the Solomon Islands and Samoa.
Ask your PCA office about the fungi Metarhizium anisopliae and Beauveria bassiana, which infect the larvae and adults.
Plant more resistant types where you can. In the Solomon Islands, Local Tall coconut was more resistant than some dwarf types.

blocks.text: Chemicals are best kept for young palms and nurseries, and only when natural enemies cannot keep up. Synthetic pyrethroids probably work but also kill the natural enemies. Follow the label and the FPA registration.

blocks.caption: Active ingredients that work. Always follow the label of an FPA registered product.
rows: plant derived, for young palms and nurseries only
plant derived, for young palms and nurseries only

blocks.title: Spray safely
blocks.text: Use only products registered with the [Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority](/blog/fertilizer-and-pesticide-authority), and follow the label for the rate, the timing and the protective clothing. Switch to a different insecticide group next time, so the pest does not learn to survive it. Our [guide to integrated pest management](/pests/integrated-pest-management) explains how.

items: Check every new palm and ornamental palm that enters the farm.
Do not move palms or fronds out of an infested district.
Keep nursery seedlings well watered, because dry periods favor the beetle.
Protect the wasps and fungi that live in your grove by avoiding broad spray campaigns.

blocks.text: Questions Farmers Ask About Coconut Leaf Beetle

items.q: How do I know it is Brontispa and not drought?
items.a: Open the young spear leaf. Brontispa damage comes with beetles and larvae inside, and it starts in the newest leaves. Drought scorch does not.
Only for a short time. PCARRD reports that the beetle returned after sprays wore off, and this is why the PCA now promotes integrated pest management.
The wasps Asecodes hispinarum, which attacks larvae, and Tetrastichus brontispae, which attacks pupae, plus the fungi Metarhizium anisopliae and Beauveria bassiana.
Seedlings in nurseries and young palms after planting. Older palms are attacked too, and lose yield.
